title: SlowFast Networks for Video Recognition
layout_note: Two horizontal pathways: the Slow lane on top (4 sparse frames into three wide blue-tinted 3-D blocks) and the Fast lane below (many dense frames into three thin green-tinted 3-D blocks); vertical lateral arrows rise from the Fast lane into the Slow lane after each stage, and both lanes end in one tall shared 'prediction' bar at the right.
grouping: No containers: the two pathways are grouped only by their horizontal rows and by tint family (pale blue blocks top, pale green blocks bottom); captions 'Low frame rate' / 'High frame rate' sit under the frame stacks.
shapes_depth: Feature tensors are thin-outlined 3-D boxes (cuboids) with a soft radial colour fill, sized to their dimensions: Slow blocks are wide and shallow (C, T), Fast blocks are narrow and deep-thin (βC, αT). Input frames are flat grey slanted parallelograms, 4 spaced apart on top and about 15 overlapping below. The prediction bar is a tall rectangle with a blue-to-green vertical gradient. Plain black straight arrows; no shadows.
proposed_highlight: The idea is carried by contrast rather than a highlight colour: the same three stages are drawn twice, wide-blue vs thin-green, with βC / αT vs C / T italic labels on the cuboid edges so the channel and temporal ratio is read off the block shapes.
lesson: Show a two-rate design by drawing the same stages twice with shape-encoded dimensions (wide shallow cuboids vs thin deep ones, labelled C,T vs βC,αT) and joining them with vertical lateral arrows, so the ratio is visible without a table.
notes: venue = arXiv (remembered venue: ICCV 2019; not printed on the arXiv first page); year = arXiv preprint year. A small 3-axis glyph (H,W up, T diagonal, C right) sits between the two lanes to key the block dimensions.

arrangement.units: two unframed horizontal lanes (Slow on top, Fast below) separated by whitespace, each a row of input frame stack plus three cuboid stages; a single tall prediction bar spans both lanes at the right
arrangement.inputs_as: stacks of flat grey slanted parallelograms standing for frames (4 sparse vs ~15 dense), captioned 'Low frame rate' / 'High frame rate'
arrangement.losses_at: none drawn; only the 'prediction' bar at the right end
arrangement.shared: the prediction head is one tall bar spanning both lanes, its gradient blending the two lane tints

insights.structure: Two unframed horizontal lanes, Slow on top and Fast below, each run frames -> three cuboid stages, and both converge into one tall prediction bar at the right edge.
insights.data: Frames are grey slanted parallelograms whose count (4 vs ~15) encodes frame rate, and feature tensors are 3-D cuboids whose width and depth encode C,T vs βC,αT, labelled in italics on their edges.
insights.emphasis: The contribution is the contrast itself: blue wide cuboids vs green thin cuboids, with the prediction bar's blue-to-green gradient showing the two pathways merging.
insights.flow: Both lanes read left to right with straight black arrows, and after each stage a vertical arrow rises from the Fast lane into the Slow lane's horizontal arrow as a lateral connection.
insights.avoid: The axis glyph floats between the lanes with no frame, and the blocks have only faint radial tints so the blue/green coding nearly disappears in print.

measured.source: computed: paperfig kb measure (non-white pixels of a <= 800 px thumbnail, white = min(R,G,B) >= 245, minus the embedded images recorded by `refs crop` (images_px; their share is photo_share, null without a record); chromatic (RGB spread > 20) and neutral pixels clustered separately by PIL median-cut + k-means (k=8 / 3); clusters within dE00 4 merged; kept if >= 0.02 of chromatic pixels / neutral ones if >= 0.03 of all non-white pixels; share = fraction of the non-photo non-white pixels)
